questions.q: What's the most important factor in deciding whether an agreement is a lease or a licence?
choices: What the parties chose to call the document
Whether the occupier has exclusive possession
Whether the rent is paid monthly or yearly
Whether the agreement was ever registered
questions.explain: Ocean Harvesters v. Quinlan Bros.: it's about intention, and exclusive possession is the key evidence. Labels don't decide it.

questions.q: An owner who holds a licence over part of their land sells the land. What happens to the licence?
choices: The buyer takes subject to it
It continues for one more year
questions.explain: A licence is a personal contractual permission, not an interest in land, so it doesn't run with the land.

questions.q: A landlord provides daily meals and a housekeeper who enters the room at will. This suggests what?
questions.explain: The occupier lacks exclusive possession, which points to a licence.

questions.q: Which arrangement IS covered by the Residential Tenancy Act?
choices: A room sharing a kitchen with the owner
A caretaker's suite in an apartment block
A furnished vacation rental for a week
questions.explain: Caretakers' and employees' units are included. Shared kitchen/bathroom with the owner, vacation rentals and terms over 20 years are excluded.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · Commercial vs residential: which rulebook?

questions.q: A florist rents a shop with an apartment above it under a single lease. Which law mainly governs?
choices: The common law and the lease
The Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act
questions.explain: Business premises with an attached dwelling under one lease are excluded from the RTA, so it's a commercial tenancy.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · Commercial vs residential: which rulebook?

questions.q: How soon must a residential landlord give the tenant a copy of the signed tenancy agreement?
questions.explain: Promptly, and in any event within 21 days.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · What must be in the agreement

questions.q: Which commercial lease must be in writing to be enforceable?
questions.explain: Law and Equity Act s.59 requires writing for leases over 3 years.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · What must be in the agreement

questions.q: A one-year commercial lease expires and nobody says anything. The tenant leaves on the last day. Was notice needed?
questions.explain: A commercial fixed term ends automatically at the end of the term.

questions.q: A one-year residential tenancy expires with no vacate clause and no new agreement. What happens?
choices: It becomes month-to-month on the same terms
It renews automatically for another full year
The tenant must move out within 30 days
questions.explain: Under s.44(3), it's deemed renewed as a month-to-month tenancy on the same terms.

questions.q: When can a residential tenancy agreement validly require the tenant to move out at the end of a fixed term?
choices: Whenever both parties have agreed to it in writing
For a sublease, or if the landlord's family moves in
Whenever the landlord is planning to sell the home
Only for fixed terms that are 6 months or shorter
questions.explain: Vacate clauses are limited to subleases and the circumstances in Regulation s.13.1 (landlord or close family occupying).

questions.q: A commercial tenant overholds after a 3-year lease at "$24,000 per year, payable $2,000 monthly". The landlord accepts rent. What tenancy probably arises?
questions.explain: An original term of a year or more with rent stated yearly usually implies a yearly tenancy (unless the lease says otherwise).

questions.q: With no lease clause, what's the usual reasonable notice to end a yearly commercial periodic tenancy?
questions.explain: Usually six months for a yearly tenancy, and one full period for weekly or monthly ones, though it's flexible.

questions.q: In Union Properties v. Johnston Terminals, what notice was found reasonable for a monthly commercial tenancy?
questions.explain: 28 days. What's reasonable depends on the circumstances.

questions.q: A seller lets the buyer move in two weeks before completion, with nothing agreed about rent. What is this?
questions.explain: A tenancy at will. The seller can still claim compensation for use and occupation unless it was agreed to be rent-free.

questions.q: What is "security of tenure" under the Residential Tenancy Act?
choices: The tenant's right to renew any lease
Tenancies end only on grounds the Act allows
The landlord's right to collect a deposit
Protection from all future rent increases
questions.explain: Landlords can end a tenancy only on grounds the Act permits; complaining about repairs isn't one.

questions.q: A tenant gets a notice for unpaid rent. How can they cancel it?
questions.explain: Paying the overdue rent within 5 days of receiving the notice makes it of no effect (or they can dispute within 5 days).
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · The landlord's notices at a glance

questions.q: How soon can a notice for non-payment of rent take effect?
choices: At least one month after receipt
At the end of the rental period
questions.explain: Not earlier than 10 days after the tenant receives it.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · The landlord's notices at a glance

questions.q: How much notice must a landlord give when ending a tenancy for cause?
questions.explain: At least one month, effective on the last day of a rental period.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · The landlord's notices at a glance

questions.q: Which is NOT a ground to end a residential tenancy for cause?
choices: Giving false information to a buyer
questions.explain: Complaining about repairs isn't cause. The Act protects security of tenure.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · The landlord's notices at a glance

questions.q: A tenant receives a Three Month Notice for landlord's use. How long do they have to dispute it?
questions.explain: 5 days (rent), 10 (cause), 15 (two-month), 21 (three-month), 30 (four-month).
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · The landlord's notices at a glance

questions.q: What happens if a tenant doesn't dispute a valid notice in time?
choices: The landlord must serve it again
questions.explain: They're conclusively presumed to accept the end of tenancy and must leave by the effective date.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · The landlord's notices at a glance

questions.q: Which is NOT required before a seller must give a Three Month Notice for a buyer's use?
choices: All subjects in the sale have been removed
The buyer has already completed the purchase
The buyer intends in good faith to occupy
The buyer asks the seller in writing
questions.explain: The notice is given before completion, once subjects are removed and the buyer asks in writing.

questions.q: Who counts as a "close family member" for landlord's or purchaser's use?
questions.explain: Parent, spouse or child, or the spouse's parent or child. Not siblings.

questions.q: A buyer wants vacant possession of a unit with a fixed term ending in 8 months. Can a Three Month Notice end it sooner?
choices: Yes, if three months' notice is given
No, not before the fixed term ends
Yes, if the buyer pays the tenant
questions.explain: Landlord's or purchaser's use notices can't take effect before the fixed term ends.

questions.q: In which building can a landlord NOT end a tenancy for their own or a purchaser's use?
choices: A house with one basement suite
A non-strata building with 5+ rental units
A strata condo owned by a single individual
A duplex that is owned entirely by one person
questions.explain: s.49(6.1): not in buildings with 5+ rental units that are non-strata or stratified but all owned by one owner.

questions.q: In the 2016 discipline case, why was the buyer's licensee suspended?
choices: They refused to show the property to buyers
The contract gave far too little notice
They lied about the rental income
They kept the tenant's security deposit
questions.explain: The contract set vacant possession on June 14 (formed May 7) with no tenancy details or notice clause: 7 days, $1,250 and a course.

questions.q: What must a landlord pay a tenant who receives a s.49 landlord's use notice?
questions.explain: One month's rent, on or before the effective date. The tenant can withhold the last month's rent.

questions.q: A buyer has the seller evict a tenant for the buyer's use, then rents the home out instead. What can the tenant claim?
questions.explain: s.51(2): 12 months' rent if the stated purpose isn't carried out (on top of the one month already paid).

questions.q: How does a landlord end a tenancy to renovate?
choices: Apply to the RTB for an order
questions.explain: s.49.2 requires an RTB order first; the landlord must prove permits, necessity and vacancy.

questions.q: Which notice applies when a landlord has permits to demolish a rental unit?
questions.explain: Demolition or conversion: Four Month Notice (dispute within 30 days).

questions.q: After receiving a landlord's use notice, how much notice must the tenant give to leave early?
questions.explain: s.50: at least 10 days' written notice. They pay rent only for days occupied and keep the compensation.

questions.q: A landlord gives notice to end a tenancy on a home-made form. Is it valid?
choices: Yes, if it's signed and dated
Yes, if the tenant received it
questions.explain: A landlord's notice is void unless it uses the approved form. A tenant's notice can be any written form.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · Form and delivery of notices

questions.q: A landlord mails a notice on March 1. When is it deemed received?
questions.explain: Mail is deemed received on the 5th day after mailing. Email, fax and door posting: the 3rd day.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · Form and delivery of notices

questions.q: When is a notice taped to the tenant's door deemed received?
questions.explain: Attaching to a door or leaving in a mailbox: the 3rd day after.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · Form and delivery of notices

questions.q: Which statement about RTB arbitrators is correct?
choices: They're not bound by legal precedent
questions.explain: They decide on the merits, aren't bound by precedent, can accept any evidence, and their decisions can be enforced as Supreme Court orders.

questions.q: Within what time must an RTB arbitrator give a written decision?
questions.explain: Within 30 days of the hearing. The decision is final and binding.

questions.q: Which lease makes the tenant pay base rent plus taxes, insurance and repairs?
questions.explain: Triple net: the tenant pays base rent plus all operating costs. A gross lease includes them in the rent.

questions.q: From a commercial tenant's point of view, which lease best protects against rising operating costs?
questions.explain: In a gross lease the landlord bears increases in operating costs until a rent review.

questions.q: How often can a residential landlord raise the same tenant's rent?
choices: Only at the end of a fixed term
questions.explain: At least 12 months after the last increase or the start of the tenancy, with 3 months' notice on the prescribed form.

questions.q: A new owner buys a rental building and wants to raise the existing tenants' rent right away. Can they?
choices: Yes, a sale resets the 12 months
No, a new landlord gets no reset
questions.explain: A change of landlord doesn't create a right to raise rent.

questions.q: How much notice is needed for a residential rent increase?
questions.explain: At least three months' written notice on the prescribed form.

questions.q: Which is no longer a ground for a residential landlord to seek an additional rent increase?
choices: Rent far below similar local units
An extraordinary rise in operating costs
A financial loss on operating costs
questions.explain: Landlords can no longer apply on the basis that rent is significantly below market.

questions.q: What's the maximum residential security deposit?
questions.explain: Half a month's rent, collected only when the agreement is made. A pet damage deposit can be another half month.

questions.q: A residential landlord neither returns the deposit nor applies to the RTB within 15 days after the tenancy ends. What may they owe?
questions.explain: s.38(6): double the deposit (and pet deposit).

questions.q: Who must return a residential tenant's deposit after the building is sold?
choices: The buyer, as the new landlord
questions.explain: Under s.93, the deposit obligation runs with the land, so buyers must collect deposits and interest from the seller.

questions.q: What's the default position on a commercial security deposit when the building is sold?
choices: It passes to the buyer automatically by law
It's the old landlord's personal obligation
It's held in trust by the RTB until the end
It's forfeited to the buyer on completion
questions.explain: At common law it's personal to the landlord, unless the sale contract transfers it (usually with a credit on the adjustments).

questions.q: Can a residential landlord seize a tenant's belongings to cover unpaid rent?
questions.explain: Distress is abolished for residential tenancies (s.26(3)). It remains available to commercial landlords.

questions.q: A commercial tenant abandons, and the landlord re-lets without telling the tenant it's on their account. What's the risk?
choices: The landlord breaches the covenant of quiet enjoyment
It may be a surrender, ending future rent claims
The landlord must refund the tenant's deposit
The tenant can then reclaim possession of it
questions.explain: Re-letting inconsistent with the tenancy can be a surrender by operation of law. Highway Properties lets a landlord terminate and claim damages if it gives notice.

questions.q: Which landlords have a statutory duty to mitigate when a tenant leaves early?
questions.explain: s.7(2) of the RTA requires both residential landlords and tenants to mitigate.

questions.q: What does the covenant of quiet enjoyment mainly protect?
choices: Freedom from every kind of noise at all times
Possession free from title claims and interference
The tenant's right to sublet the premises freely
Protection from any increases in the rent
questions.explain: It protects against defects in title and substantial interference with use, not just noise.

questions.q: Without the tenant's consent, what written notice does a residential landlord need to enter?
questions.explain: At least 24 hours and not more than 30 days before, with a reasonable purpose and a time between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m.

questions.q: Between what hours may a residential landlord schedule entry (unless the tenant agrees otherwise)?
questions.explain: 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.

questions.q: A commercial landlord refuses to let a new tenant in at the start of the lease. What's the tenant's remedy?
questions.explain: Interesse termini: the commercial tenant can only sue for damages. A residential tenant can get an order of possession.
questions.ref: Lesson 10 · Getting possession at the start (interesse termini)

questions.q: What does caveat lessee mean in commercial leasing?
choices: The landlord must keep premises fit
No implied landlord duty to repair
The tenant must make all repairs
questions.explain: Let the tenant beware: absent a lease term, the landlord needn't repair unfurnished premises.

questions.q: A residential tenant knew the heating was faulty when they signed. Is the landlord still obliged to repair it?
choices: The landlord must keep premises fit
No implied landlord duty to repair
The tenant must make all the repairs
questions.explain: s.32: the duty applies whether or not the tenant knew of the problem, and can't be contracted out of.

questions.q: When can a residential tenant pay for emergency repairs and deduct the cost?
choices: No, because the tenant accepted it
Yes, regardless of what they knew
Only if the tenancy agreement says so
Only if the fault counts as an emergency
questions.explain: If repairs aren't made within a reasonable time after two or more attempts to reach the emergency contact. Receipts required.

questions.q: A commercial lease says only "the Tenant shall not assign." Can the tenant sublet?
choices: Any time any repair is needed
After trying the contact at least twice
Only once they have an RTB order
questions.explain: Courts read restrictions narrowly; a ban on assignment doesn't stop a sublease.

questions.q: What makes an arrangement a sublease rather than an assignment?
questions.explain: The tenant must keep part of the term (typically at least the last day); otherwise it's an assignment.

questions.q: Can a residential landlord charge a fee to consent to a sublet?
choices: Yes, up to half a month's rent
Yes, if the term is 6+ months
questions.explain: A residential landlord can never charge for consent, and can't unreasonably withhold it for fixed terms of 6 months or more.

questions.q: A tenancy agreement from 2016 bans tobacco smoking and says nothing about cannabis. What applies?
choices: Cannabis smoking is restricted the same way
Cannabis smoking needs the landlord's approval
The whole tenancy agreement is void
questions.explain: For agreements before Oct 17, 2018, tobacco restrictions are deemed to cover cannabis.
